state_rules.absent: Absent means no context or retrieval channel took part in the run at all.
state_rules.default: No default exists: the content is whatever the run supplied; there is nothing to fall back to.
state_rules.disabled: Not applicable as a value; a disabled channel is recorded as absent where absence is permitted.
state_rules.unknown: Never recorded. If the bytes cannot be obtained the record is not written (I10, §10).

unobservable_declaration.evidence: Phase 0, executed 2026-08-08 under §3.0 containment, read the whole of backend/app/ and found no decoding parameter at either call site. Reading vendor SDK source would not settle it either, because provider-side defaults are not in the SDK; and establishing them by observation would require a live provider call, which D3 forbids. No client-side default is therefore verifiable.
unobservable_declaration.reason: No decoding parameter is set anywhere in the repository: the OpenAI adapter passes only model, input and text.format; the Gemini adapter passes only model, contents and a config carrying system_instruction, response_mime_type and response_json_schema. No temperature, top_p, top_k, seed, max_tokens or stop sequence exists at any call site. The effective values are resolved inside the vendor SDK and, for server-side defaults, inside the provider.

state_rules.default: No default: the order is a literal in the orchestrator and is always present.
state_rules.disabled: Not representable: dispatch always occurs when there is more than one engine.
state_rules.unknown: Never: the values are constants readable at emission without any call.

keys.meaning: Whether dispatch order can be changed by configuration at run time. False: the order is a literal in the orchestrator.
How the engines are dispatched. Sequential: the second engine is called only after the first returns.

default_resolution.note: A string rather than an array because a basis parameter value is always a string (§4.2B).

keys.meaning: The dispatch order as a comma-separated engine list, in call order, with no spaces.

state_rules.default: No default: the absence of a fallback path is a property of the code, readable without any call.
state_rules.disabled: This dimension's normal state: enabled=false is the disabled state, carried as content rather than as absence.
state_rules.unknown: Never: whether a fallback path exists is decidable by reading the orchestrator.

default_resolution.note: Configured absence of a fallback is a configured state with content, not an absence (§4.2B).

keys.meaning: Whether any fallback path exists. False: no substitute provider, model or degraded mode is attempted.
What happens when a provider call fails. Propagate: the error is raised and the run terminates for that engine.

content_rule.absence_case: Absent means no prompt channel distinct from the workload exists for this run at all.
content_rule.byte_coverage: The exact UTF-8 bytes of the fully assembled prompt as handed to the provider adapter — system instruction and user prompt concatenated in the order sent, with no re-encoding and no normalization.
content_rule.empty_case: Present and empty means a prompt channel exists and carried zero bytes: byte_length 0 with the digest of the empty byte sequence, computed and never transcribed.

unobservable_declaration.evidence: Phase 0 grep across backend/app/ returned no retry or backoff setting. Retry behaviour is transport-level: even a live call would not report the policy that governed it, so no observation could establish the effective value.
unobservable_declaration.reason: No retry, backoff or attempt policy is configured at any call site; whatever retry behaviour occurs is internal to the vendor SDK and is not reported back in any response.

unobservable_declaration.evidence: Phase 0 found no termination setting at either call site, and both adapters discard the provider response object, retaining only text and token counts — so even a reported finish reason would not survive to emission.
unobservable_declaration.reason: No stop sequence, max-token bound or other termination control is configured. Why generation stopped is decided by the provider and is not carried back into any structure the repository retains.

unobservable_declaration.evidence: Phase 0 grep across backend/app/ found exactly that one occurrence and no provider-call timeout. Like retry, an effective timeout is transport-level and is not reported in any response.
unobservable_declaration.reason: No timeout or deadline is configured at any provider call site. The only timeout in the package is t.join(timeout=2) on the SSE worker thread, which governs a UI stream and not a provider call.

content_rule.byte_coverage: The exact UTF-8 bytes of the canonical serialization of the workload document as submitted to the run — the question and any run-level workload parameters, excluding retrieved context and excluding the assembled prompt.
content_rule.empty_case: A zero-length workload is representable (byte_length 0) but cannot occur: the orchestrator rejects an empty or whitespace question before any call.
